newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SocGen fund unit aims to be Asia top-gun.
newsitem.headline: SocGen fund unit aims to be Asia top-gun.

text.p: Societe Generale Asset Management (Asia) Pte Lte (SGAMA) aims to be among Asia's top billion-dollar asset fund managers within two or three years, company officials said on Wednesday.

"We definitely want to be a major player in this area and plans to be the billionaire asset management in two to three years timeframe," Laurent Bertiau, managing director and chief executive officer told reporters.
Two years after setting up operations in Asia, SGAMA now manages a fund of Singapore $334.2 million as of July 29, 1997, raised in Europe and invested in Asia, outside Japan.

Francis Bijon, Bertiau's predessor, said about S$150 million was invested in the Asia Pacific region, S$150 million in emerging Asia, about S$20 million in the Greater China fund and about S$10 million in the Indian subcontinent.
SGAMA also manages US$300 million raised from public authorities and institutional investors in Asia, mainly Singapore, Hong Kong and Taiwan.
"There is a very strong commitment from Paris headquarters to increase and develop the international presence our asset management," Bertiau said.
"Singapore will be the focal point of this strategy in Asia," he said, adding that Singapore's responsibility excludes Japan and South Korea.
To achieve this goal, the group will be launching new funds including small-cap funds, emerging market funds and close-end funds, Bertiau said.

"Right now, most of our sources are from Europe investors. We want a better balance between assets coming from Europe and assets flowing to Asia. That is why we will expand our Asia market strategy," Bertiau said.
The company plans to hire a regional marketing manager and to expand into Taiwan and Hong Kong by October.
Expansion in Japan will either be in the form of an investment advisory company, investment trust (IT) company or marketing offshore funds, Bertiau said.
"In the long term, we have in mind to set up the IT or investment advisory company. But initially, it will be through marketing offshore units," Bertiau said.
